key_insight: SPEAK-NORM detects early ALS-related speech changes by learning what healthy speech should look like, then flagging deviations from that normative model.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier, scalable screening for ALS using routine speech recordings, potentially helping identify patients before major diagnostic delay.
method: Trains a conditional variational autoencoder only on healthy speech, conditioned on age and sex.
Quantifies deviation from the healthy speech manifold using latent features and reconstruction error.
Uses a calibrated linear SVM to classify subjects with subject-disjoint validation.
evidence_signal: On the VOC-ALS dataset (n=153), the model achieved 98% accuracy with balanced sensitivity and specificity, and it also generalized well across task settings and external neurodegenerative cohorts.
watch_item: Results are promising but come from relatively small cohorts, so broader validation is still needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Normative Speech Modeling for ALS Diagnosis with Application to Other Neurodegenerative Diseases
